## Overview

Add initial PyTorch-native support for [Lfm2BidirectionalModel](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-Embedding-350M) with minimal changes to the existing LFM2 implementation. 

Implement noncausal short conv over packed sequences, with request-boundary and padding
masking, encoder-only attention, and CLS pooling.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Findings marked 🟡 are optional suggestions and need no follow-up push.

<!-- bhrv:b03962d54311ff16 -->

🔴 With `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` on the default V2 runner, LFM2.5 embeddings become batch-dependent: the conv mixes neighbouring requests and padding rows. The new conv reads `forward_context.is_padding` with no gate. Model Runner V2 only refreshes that mask when `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` is set (gpu/model_runner.py:1378). Otherwise it holds the all-True fill left by CUDA graph capture. Fix: always pass an accurate real-token mask to this conv, whatever MoE env vars are set. For example, fill `is_padding` unconditionally in V2 `prepare_inputs`, or derive the real-token count from the forward context. Every other reader of the mask gates on that env var.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is an operator who sets `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` while serving `Lfm2BidirectionalModel` on Model Runner V2. In V2, `prepare_inputs` (v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1377-1380) fills `input_buffers.is_padding` only under that env var. It still passes the buffer to `set_forward_context(is_padding=input_batch.is_padding)` (model_runner.py:2042). CUDA graph capture runs `input_buffers.is_padding.fill_(True)` on the whole buffer (gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:720,747). As a result, every real token reaches `_bidirectional_conv1d` marked as padding. At lfm2.py:267 all sequence ids then become -2, so the `same_sequence` mask never separates requests. On the base branch nothing in this model reads `is_padding`. Every existing consumer gates on `envs.VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING`. The new test only runs with the default value of 1.

**Verification:** `prepare_inputs` refreshes the mask only under that env var (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1377-1380). CUDA graph capture runs `input_buffers.is_padding.fill_(True)` (cudagraph_utils.py:720, 747). The new code reads that mask with no gate. The new batch-invariance test does not catch this because it runs with the default env.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

+def _bidirectional_conv1d(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    is_padding: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Same-padding depthwise convolution over packed, complete sequences."""
+    kernel_size = weight.shape[-1]
+    padding = kernel_size // 2
+    # Each encoder request starts at position zero. For packed requests
+    # x = [a0, a1, a2, b0, b1], positions = [0, 1, 2, 0, 1] gives
+    # sequence_ids = [1, 1, 1, 2, 2].
+    sequence_ids = (positions == 0).cumsum(0)
+    if is_padding is not None:
+        # Keep runtime padding (e.g. CUDA graph padding) distinct from real requests.
+        sequence_ids = sequence_ids.masked_fill(is_padding, -2)
+    # With kernel_size=3 and no runtime padding, the example becomes:
+    # padded_ids = [-1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, -1]
+    # padded_x   = [ 0, a0, a1, a2, b0, b1, 0]
+    padded_ids = F.pad(sequence_ids, (padding, padding), value=-1)
+    padded_x = F.pad(x, (0, 0, padding, padding))
+    output = torch.zeros_like(x, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for tap in range(kernel_size):
+        # Exclude neighbors across request boundaries (e.g. a2 and b0).
+        same_sequence = padded_ids[tap : tap + x.shape[0]] == sequence_ids
+        values = padded_x[tap : tap + x.shape[0]].float()
+        values = values.masked_fill(~same_sequence[:, None], 0)
+        output = output + values * weight[:, 0, tap].float()
+    if bias is not None:
+        output = output + bias.float()
+    return output.to(x.dtype)
+

+        config: Lfm2Config,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",

+        super().__init__()

+        self.conv = ColumnParallelLinear(
+            config.conv_L_cache, dim, bias=config.conv_bias, prefix=f"{prefix}.conv1d"
+        )
+        self.conv.weight.data = self.conv.weight.data.unsqueeze(1)

+            [dim] * 3,
+            bias=config.conv_bias,

+            dim,

+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.out_proj",
+        )
+

nodes.body:
🟡 (optional) Users of the new LFM2.5 embedding model only get the "embed" task. Per-token embeddings ("token_embed") are rejected, unlike other embedding models such as BERT, CLIP and SigLIP. `pooler_for_embed` builds a bare `SequencePooler` whose `EmbeddingPoolerHead` supports only {"embed"}. Fix: build the pooler with `DispatchPooler.for_embedding(pooler_config)`, the same way `bert.py:525`, `clip.py:836` and `siglip.py:946` do, so both "embed" and "token_embed" are available.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`Lfm2BidirectionalModel.__init__` (lfm2.py:504) sets `self.pooler = pooler_for_embed(pooler_config)`. `pooler_for_embed` (pooler/seqwise/poolers.py:97) returns a `SequencePooler` with an `EmbeddingPoolerHead`. That head's `get_supported_tasks` (seqwise/heads.py:56-57) returns only {"embed"}, and `SequencePooler.get_supported_tasks` (poolers.py:69-74) intersects with it. So a request through `LLM.encode(..., pooling_task="token_embed")`, or the token-embedding pooling API, is rejected as an unsupported task for this model. Every other dense embedding model in the tree builds its pooler with `DispatchPooler.for_embedding` (special.py:29-35), which serves both "token_embed" and "embed". This is a new architecture, so there is no base-branch behaviour; the gap is relative to how other embedding models behave.

**Verification:** lfm2.py:504 sets `self.pooler = pooler_for_embed(pooler_config)`, a bare pooler with no dispatcher. `EmbeddingPoolerHead.get_supported_tasks` in seqwise/heads.py returns only `{"embed"}`. So the model advertises only "embed", and `token_embed` requests are rejected as unsupported. Among standalone embedding models, lfm2.py is the only one that uses bare `pooler_for_embed`.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

nodes.body: Thanks for catching this. I am not sure whether always fill an accurate real-token mask might have any unnecessary impact on the performance of a dense model, So I added an optional model capability  `requires_padding_mask`, which defaults to False, and enabled it for `Lfm2BidirectionalModel`. Model Runner V2 now refreshes the mask when either the model requires it or `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` is enabled. This makes the convolution’s correctness independent of the MoE optimization flag while preserving conditional updates for other models.  could u also help cc. @DarkLight1337 thank u very much.

 from ...utils import check_embeddings_close
 
 
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kernel_size", [3, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_padding_tokens", [0, 3])
+def test_lfm2_bidirectional_conv_respects_sequence_boundaries(
+    dtype, kernel_size, num_padding_tokens
+):
+    """Packed short sequences must match independent noncausal convolutions."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.models.lfm2 import _bidirectional_conv1d
+
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    lengths = [1, 1, 7, 2]
+    inputs = [torch.randn(n, 8, generator=generator).to(dtype) for n in lengths]
+    weight = torch.randn(8, 1, kernel_size, generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    bias = torch.randn(8, generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    expected = []
+    for x in inputs:
+        y = torch.nn.functional.conv1d(
+            x.T[None].float(),
+            weight.float(),
+            bias.float(),
+            padding=kernel_size // 2,
+            groups=8,
+        )
+        expected.append(y[0, :, : len(x)].T.to(dtype))
+
+    packed = torch.cat(inputs)
+    positions = torch.cat([torch.arange(n) for n in lengths])
+    is_padding = None
+    if num_padding_tokens:
+        # Graph padding may retain positions and values from an earlier batch.
+        packed = torch.cat([packed, torch.full((num_padding_tokens, 8), float("nan"))])
+        positions = torch.cat([positions, torch.arange(2, 2 + num_padding_tokens)])
+        is_padding = torch.arange(len(packed)) >= sum(lengths)
+    actual = _bidirectional_conv1d(
+        packed.to(dtype),
+        weight,
+        bias,
+        positions,
+        is_padding,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual[: sum(lengths)], torch.cat(expected))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enforce_eager", [True, False])

inline_comments.body:
🔴 With `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` on the default V2 runner, LFM2.5 embeddings become batch-dependent: the conv mixes neighbouring requests and padding rows. The new conv reads `forward_context.is_padding` with no gate. Model Runner V2 only refreshes that mask when `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` is set (gpu/model_runner.py:1378). Otherwise it holds the all-True fill left by CUDA graph capture. Fix: always pass an accurate real-token mask to this conv, whatever MoE env vars are set. For example, fill `is_padding` unconditionally in V2 `prepare_inputs`, or derive the real-token count from the forward context. Every other reader of the mask gates on that env var.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is an operator who sets `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` while serving `Lfm2BidirectionalModel` on Model Runner V2. In V2, `prepare_inputs` (v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1377-1380) fills `input_buffers.is_padding` only under that env var. It still passes the buffer to `set_forward_context(is_padding=input_batch.is_padding)` (model_runner.py:2042). CUDA graph capture runs `input_buffers.is_padding.fill_(True)` on the whole buffer (gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:720,747). As a result, every real token reaches `_bidirectional_conv1d` marked as padding. At lfm2.py:267 all sequence ids then become -2, so the `same_sequence` mask never separates requests. On the base branch nothing in this model reads `is_padding`. Every existing consumer gates on `envs.VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING`. The new test only runs with the default value of 1.

**Verification:** `prepare_inputs` refreshes the mask only under that env var (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1377-1380). CUDA graph capture runs `input_buffers.is_padding.fill_(True)` (cudagraph_utils.py:720, 747). The new code reads that mask with no gate. The new batch-invariance test does not catch this because it runs with the default env.

</details>

inline_comments.body:
🟡 (optional) Users of the new LFM2.5 embedding model only get the "embed" task. Per-token embeddings ("token_embed") are rejected, unlike other embedding models such as BERT, CLIP and SigLIP. `pooler_for_embed` builds a bare `SequencePooler` whose `EmbeddingPoolerHead` supports only {"embed"}. Fix: build the pooler with `DispatchPooler.for_embedding(pooler_config)`, the same way `bert.py:525`, `clip.py:836` and `siglip.py:946` do, so both "embed" and "token_embed" are available.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`Lfm2BidirectionalModel.__init__` (lfm2.py:504) sets `self.pooler = pooler_for_embed(pooler_config)`. `pooler_for_embed` (pooler/seqwise/poolers.py:97) returns a `SequencePooler` with an `EmbeddingPoolerHead`. That head's `get_supported_tasks` (seqwise/heads.py:56-57) returns only {"embed"}, and `SequencePooler.get_supported_tasks` (poolers.py:69-74) intersects with it. So a request through `LLM.encode(..., pooling_task="token_embed")`, or the token-embedding pooling API, is rejected as an unsupported task for this model. Every other dense embedding model in the tree builds its pooler with `DispatchPooler.for_embedding` (special.py:29-35), which serves both "token_embed" and "embed". This is a new architecture, so there is no base-branch behaviour; the gap is relative to how other embedding models behave.

**Verification:** lfm2.py:504 sets `self.pooler = pooler_for_embed(pooler_config)`, a bare pooler with no dispatcher. `EmbeddingPoolerHead.get_supported_tasks` in seqwise/heads.py returns only `{"embed"}`. So the model advertises only "embed", and `token_embed` requests are rejected as unsupported. Among standalone embedding models, lfm2.py is the only one that uses bare `pooler_for_embed`.

</details>

inline_comments.body: Thanks for catching this. I am not sure whether always fill an accurate real-token mask might have any unnecessary impact on the performance of a dense model, So I added an optional model capability  `requires_padding_mask`, which defaults to False, and enabled it for `Lfm2BidirectionalModel`. Model Runner V2 now refreshes the mask when either the model requires it or `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` is enabled. This makes the convolution’s correctness independent of the MoE optimization flag while preserving conditional updates for other models.  could u also help cc. @DarkLight1337 thank u very much.
